transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what brings you here today?

Well, doctor, I... I guess I came in because things have just been so unsettling lately, and I just don't know what to do about it anymore. I work as a personal care aide, you know, helping folks out, and it's a very hard job. It takes a lot out of you, being on your feet and caring for people all day. So when I go home to my little studio apartment, I really just need some peace and quiet to recharge. 

But lately... well, I keep hearing these voices. And I don't mean like a radio left on next door or people talking out on the street. I mean it is as clear as somebody standing right there in my little studio with me. They keep saying my name, just over and over, and they keep telling me my work is being judged. Which just gets me so worked up and upset because I do right by my clients, I work so hard for them, but these voices are just right there judging everything I do. 

And the thing that really gets me is, I'll look around, I'll check the door, and the house is completely quiet. There is absolutely nobody there. Just me. But I hear them so plain, like they're right over my shoulder in the empty room, and it's just... it's driving me to my wit's end, having to deal with that when I'm just trying to get a moment of rest in my own home. I just can't take the judging when nobody is even in the room with me.
When you hear these voices, do they sound like they are coming from inside your head or from somewhere outside, like in the room with you?

Oh, definitely outside. Like I was saying, it's not a thought. You know how you think to yourself, 'Oh, I need to pick up some milk at the store,' and it's just your own voice inside your mind? It is nothing like that. It is entirely outside, right there in the room with me. Like... like if you were standing right next to my kitchen counter right now. 

My studio is very small, you see, it's just the one main room and a little bathroom off to the side, so there aren't a lot of places for someone to hide. But these voices... they are coming from the actual, physical space of the room. I'll be sitting on my sofa, resting my feet because they just ache so badly after a long shift lifting and bathing clients, and I'll hear it coming right from the corner by the radiator. Just saying my name, plain as day, and telling me my work is being judged. 

And I'll whip my head around, thinking maybe the building manager let himself in, or maybe somebody somehow got up the fire escape, but the house is just dead quiet. The deadbolt is locked. There is absolutely nobody there but me. But the sound hits my ears just like your voice is hitting my ears right this second. It's not in my head at all, doctor, it's out there in the air, echoing in my little apartment, judging me when I'm just trying to have a quiet cup of tea by myself.
Have you ever seen things that others don't see, or experienced any other unusual senses like smelling something that isn't there or feeling something touching you when nothing is?

No, no, I haven't seen anything that isn't there. I mean, my eyesight isn't what it used to be, I need reading glasses for the fine print on the medication bottles at work, but no, no visions or anything like that. And I haven't smelled anything strange either, just the usual city smells coming through the window, maybe someone cooking cabbage down the hall, but nothing out of the ordinary. And I haven't felt anything touching me, thank goodness, because that would just be too much on top of everything else. 

It's really just the voices, doctor. Like I said when I first sat down, I came in because I keep hearing these voices, clear as somebody standing right there in my little studio. It's just the voices saying my name, over and over, and telling me my work is being judged. And it's so frustrating because, like I said, the house is completely quiet and nobody is there. I'll be sitting there, trying to relax, and it's just this constant judging about my work. I don't see anyone, I don't feel anyone, but I hear them. Just the hearing. And that's quite enough, let me tell you, it's more than enough to deal with when you're already exhausted from a long day.

Have you ever had any beliefs or thoughts that others might find unusual or hard to understand, like feeling that you have special powers, or that someone is controlling your thoughts, or that certain things in the world have special meaning only you can understand?

Well, I don't know anything about special powers or anything like that. I'm just a regular woman trying to pay her rent, doctor. But... well, there was this whole situation, and I still say I was right about it, even if nobody else wanted to hear it or believe me. 

See, I do a little painting on the side. Watercolors, mostly. Just little things, flowers and trees, that I do on my tiny kitchen table when I have a spare minute. Which isn't often, let me tell you, with the hours I pull at the agency. And I usually have my client papers spread out on that same table—timesheets, care logs, medication schedules, all that heavy paperwork you have to keep track of when you're an aide, because if you don't document every single thing, they act like you didn't do it at all. 

Anyway, a while back, I got it in my head—well, not just in my head, I knew it for an absolute fact—that the other home-care agency across town, the ones who drive those little green vans, and some people from the public library down the street, that they were watching my paintings and my client papers. 

I know how that sounds. I do. My sister, and even my neighbor Mrs. Higgins, they looked at me like I had grown a second head when I tried to warn them about it. They kept saying, 'Why on earth would the library ladies care about your little watercolors or your care logs? It makes no sense.' They told me I was just overtired from working too many double shifts. But they just didn't understand what was really going on, because they weren't the ones being targeted. 

Those people from the other agency and the library, they were watching my things to steal a chance that was meant for me. A really big opportunity. I don't know exactly how they were doing the watching, maybe through the windows or something else, but I could feel it, just like I know I'm sitting in this chair right now. They wanted to take this chance away from me, and they were using the library people to help them snoop on my private things. And even when folks told me it made absolutely no sense and told me to just put my papers in a drawer and forget about it, I still knew they were doing it. I mean, you can't just talk someone out of the truth, can you? I'd be sitting there, just trying to paint a nice picture of a daffodil to take my mind off my aching feet and the stress of the day, and I'd just know they were out there, plotting to steal my chance right out from under me. It's just exhausting, doctor, having to guard your own paperwork in your own home.
Do you feel that your belief about the people watching your paintings and papers is something you know to be absolutely true, even though others say there’s no reason to believe it?

Oh, absolutely. One hundred percent. It is not just some passing thought, doctor, it is the absolute truth. 

Like I was saying just a minute ago, I got it in my head—well, people say 'got it in your head' like it's some silly daydream, but I didn't just imagine it, I *knew* it. I knew for a fact that the other home-care agency and those people from the library down the street were watching my paintings and my client papers. And they weren't just being nosey, either. They were watching my things to steal a chance that was meant for me. A really big chance. 

And it's exactly like you said, about people not believing it. Because even when folks told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. My sister would sit right there in my kitchen and say I was talking nonsense and tell me to just put my watercolors away, but you can't just tell someone the sky is green when they know it's blue, can you? I mean, when you work as an aide, you don't get a lot of big opportunities handed to you in this life. You're on your feet all day, lifting people heavier than you, cleaning up messes, and you're just exhausted down to your bones. So when a chance finally comes your way, of course you're going to notice when somebody is trying to snatch it right out from under you. 

So yes, I know it to be true. I don't care if Mrs. Higgins or my sister or the whole world tells me there's no reason to believe it, because I lived it. I knew they were watching me to steal my chance, and nothing anybody says is going to change the facts of what was going on right there in my own apartment.
Do you feel that the voices you hear are part of a larger pattern of being watched or targeted, like what you described with the people from the other agency and the library?

Well, no... I don't think so. I mean, I never really put the two together like that, doctor. The voices, they're just... they're just voices in my apartment. Like I said, they just say my name and tell me my work is being judged, you know, criticizing how I do my job. Like maybe they think I didn't turn a client right in their bed, or I didn't fill out the medication schedule fast enough. Which is just ridiculous because I am very, very thorough with my logs. 

But those library people and the ones from the other agency with the green vans, they aren't talking to me. They're not the ones judging my work out loud, they're just... sneaking around. Watching my papers and my watercolors to steal my opportunity. It feels like two completely different headaches, if you want to know the truth. It's like I have to deal with the library people spying on me, trying to take what's mine, and then completely separate from that, I have to sit in my own quiet kitchen and listen to these voices picking apart my workday. 

And let me tell you, it is exhausting having to deal with both of them. You try working a double shift, lifting people who are twice your size, cleaning up after folks who can't even get to the bathroom on their own, your feet swelling up in your shoes until you can barely walk. And then you come home to your tiny studio just wanting a single moment of peace to paint a little flower or a tree, and you've got the library people watching you on one hand, and then these voices judging you on the other. But no, I haven't noticed them being part of the same thing at all. They aren't working together or anything like that. The voices don't seem to care about my big chance, they just want to tear down my hard work as an aide. It's really just two different awful things happening to me at the exact same time, which just doesn't seem fair, does it? You'd think a regular person just trying to pay her rent could get a break.
Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something was happening or was true, that others might not understand or agree with, even if you couldn't prove it to them?

Well, doctor, isn't that exactly what I've been trying to tell you this whole time? I feel like we're going in circles a little bit here, but yes, that is exactly what I've been saying about the whole situation. It's just like I was telling you before—I got it in my head that the other home-care agency, the ones with the green vans, and some people from the library down the street were watching my paintings and my client papers. 

And you ask about people not agreeing with me or not being able to prove it... well, that's the whole frustrating part of it! I mean, I don't have a photograph of them doing it. I can't just hand you or my sister a piece of paper that says, 'Look, here is the proof.' But I know what I know. They were watching my things to steal a chance that was meant for me. A really, really big chance. 

I tried to explain this to people. I sat right there at my little kitchen table, surrounded by my watercolors and my heavy care logs, and I tried to tell my sister and Mrs. Higgins what was going on. And they just looked at me like I was speaking a foreign language. They kept telling me it made absolutely no sense. They'd say, 'Why would they care about your timesheets or your little flower paintings? You're just tired from working too many shifts.' 

But even when folks told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. You don't just stop believing the truth just because someone else can't see it, do you? Especially when you're the one living it, working yourself to the bone every single day, lifting heavy clients, just trying to make rent, and then you finally get an opportunity and people are trying to steal it right out from under you. So yes, that's exactly what I've experienced. People just don't understand, and I can't exactly prove it to them in a court of law, but that doesn't make it any less true.

Have you had times when these experiences—like hearing voices or feeling watched—happened even when things in your life were otherwise calm and stable, not just during stressful periods at work or other difficult times?

Well, calm is... I mean, I don't know if I'd ever call my life completely calm, doctor, because like I said, working as an aide is just a heavy, heavy load. You're always on your feet, always taking care of someone else's needs before your own. But if you mean times when I wasn't all stressed out or going a million miles a minute, then yes. Actually, yes, I have. 

There was this one stretch... it was right after my energy finally dropped. I had been, you know, just very energized for a bit, but then my energy just sort of leveled out and went down. I was actually sleeping more normally again. Getting a full night's rest, closing my eyes at a decent hour, waking up feeling regular instead of all wound up. I thought to myself, okay, finally, a little peace and quiet. I can just do my shifts, come home, do my watercolors, get my sleep. Just a normal, stable routine, right? 

But it didn't make a lick of difference. Even with me sleeping fine and having my energy back down to a normal level, the whole thing kept going. For several weeks, actually! Several weeks of just... well, it was exhausting. The voices were still right there in my quiet apartment, judging everything I did, picking apart my work and my care logs just like before. And that whole situation—my belief that those people were judging or tracking my work? That didn't stop either. 

You'd think if it was just stress or being tired, it would go away when you get some good sleep, right? That's what my sister kept telling me. She'd sit there and say, 'Just get some sleep, you're just overworked, it'll all blow over.' But I was sleeping! I was sleeping perfectly fine, my energy was completely normal, and for weeks and weeks, I still had to deal with the voices and the tracking. So it's not just stress, doctor. It doesn't matter if my life is stable or if I'm getting my rest, they just won't leave me be. It just proves that it's really happening, don't you think? Because if it was just in my head from being tired, a good eight hours of sleep would have fixed it, but it didn't change a thing.
Do you feel that your belief about being watched and having your work judged is completely true, and do you hold onto it no matter what others say or how much they try to convince you otherwise?

Well, doctor, I really feel like I'm repeating myself here, because I swear I just went over this with you, but yes. Absolutely yes. I know what I know. Like I was saying before, I got it in my head—and I say that, but I mean I know it for an absolute fact—that the other home-care agency, you know, the ones driving those big green vans that they always park terribly, and some of those people from the library were watching my paintings and my client papers. They were doing it to steal a chance that was meant for me. A really big opportunity that I earned by working my fingers to the bone, lifting heavy people, cleaning up messes all day long, just trying to keep my head above water. 

And you ask if I hold onto it no matter what people say. Yes, I do, because why would I let someone else tell me what I'm living through? I told my sister, I told Mrs. Higgins from down the hall, and they both just tried to convince me otherwise. They would sit right at my kitchen table, drinking the coffee I made them, and tell me to my face that it made absolutely no sense. They kept asking why anyone from a library or another care agency would care about my little flower paintings or my daily care logs. They just went on and on trying to make me feel like I was making it all up just because I was tired from picking up extra shifts. 

But honestly, it doesn't matter how much they try to convince me it's not real, or how much they say it doesn't make sense. Even when folks told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. I still know it. You can't just erase the truth just because other people are too blind to see it. When you are the one putting in the hard work, day in and day out, and you see people sneaking around your things, trying to take the one good chance you have... well, you don't just let go of that just because your sister thinks you need a nap. So yes, I believe it completely, because it is completely true, no matter how many times I have to sit here and explain it.

Have you ever had a period of time where your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable, where you felt more energetic or needed less sleep than usual, maybe even to the point of being restless or unable to sit still?

Oh, doctor, let me tell you about that, because it’s a whole rollercoaster, it really is. You ask about feeling high or excited or not sleeping... well, yes, I definitely get exactly like that. There are these stretches where I just feel... well, 'bright' is the best word for it. I go from feeling so bright and, honestly, chosen. Like I’ve been picked for something truly special, you know? I’ll get all these ideas going a mile a minute, and I just feel like Greenville can’t hold all my plans! I’ll be up half the night, pacing around my little kitchen, looking at my watercolors and thinking about how I'm going to do all these massive things, and I don't even feel tired. I just feel like I have electricity running right through my veins, and I can't sit in a chair for more than two minutes without having to jump up and do something, fix something, plan something. 

But the thing is... it’s not always a happy, productive feeling. It’s like that electricity gets too hot, if that makes sense. Because I can go right from feeling on top of the world to just being so, so agitated. I mean, I will just snap hard at someone over a small thing. Just the tiniest little thing! Like, I'll be at work, and one of my regular clients—and I love my clients, I really do, I give them my absolute all—but they might just ask me to repeat myself because they didn't hear me over the television or whatever. And instead of just saying it again like I usually would, I just snap. I bite their head off over nothing. It’s like I have absolutely zero patience because my brain is moving so incredibly fast and they're just moving so slow, and it just makes me so irritable I can barely stand to be in my own skin. So, yes, I know exactly what you mean by that. It's exhausting, honestly, going from feeling like I'm going to conquer the world to just being furious over a simple question.
Can you think of a time when someone gave you clear evidence that your belief about being watched was not true? If so, did that change your mind at all?

Well doctor, I feel like a broken record, I really do, because we just touched on this, but it is so important you understand exactly how this goes. My sister, bless her heart, she really tries to play detective. She came over just last Tuesday, or maybe it was Wednesday, no, it was Tuesday because I remember the garbage trucks were making an absolute racket outside. Anyway, she came over and she brought all these printouts she made at her job. She had schedules, and she had some map from the internet showing where the other home-care agency parks their vans, and she even went down to the library and asked them about their staff shifts. She laid all this out on my coffee table, right next to my watercolor brushes and my water cups, and she pointed at it all, telling me it was absolute proof that nobody was anywhere near my building. 

Mrs. Higgins did the exact same thing, pointing at my front door and telling me the deadbolt wasn't scratched, so nobody could have gotten inside to look at anything. They both thought this so-called clear evidence was going to just magically snap me out of it. 

But did it change my mind? Not for a single second. Because like I said before, I got it in my head that the other home-care agency and some of those people from the library were watching my paintings and my client papers to steal a chance that was meant for me. I know it for a fact. And even when folks told me it made no sense, and even with my sister tapping on her little printouts and Mrs. Higgins going on about door locks, I still knew they were doing it. You just cannot wave a piece of paper in my face and tell me my own life is a lie. I am fifty-five years old, I have worked as a personal care aide for years, and I know when my client logs have been shuffled through. I know when someone is trying to take what is mine, and no amount of maps or schedules is going to make me ignore the truth of what I am living through every single day.

Can you think of a time when your belief about being watched or having your work judged occurred completely on its own, without being tied to how you were feeling emotionally or how much stress you were under at the time?

Well, you know, people always want to blame stress. They think, oh, she's just working too many double shifts, she's lifting Mr. Henderson who weighs a good two hundred pounds and she's just exhausted. Or they think it's because I get in one of those bright, electric moods I was just telling you about, where I'm pacing the kitchen all night and not sleeping a wink. But no, doctor, that's not it at all. It's not just my mood playing tricks on me, and I can prove it to you. 

Because I remember, very clearly, there was this one stretch... let's see, it was right after one of those really high-energy times. My energy had finally dropped back down, you know? The electricity was gone. I wasn't buzzing around the apartment anymore. I was actually sleeping normally again, getting a solid seven or eight hours, waking up, going to work, coming home, making my chamomile tea... just a regular, quiet routine. I wasn't feeling high or agitated or irritable at all. I felt completely level. 

But those people from the library and the other agency? They didn't stop. And the voices—because, yes, I hear them talking about it, whispering and commenting on my client logs and my watercolors—the voices and that absolute certainty that they were judging and tracking my work, well, that just kept right on going. It didn't stop just because I finally got some sleep. It kept going for several weeks, completely on its own, even when I was perfectly calm. I would wake up, fully rested, feeling totally fine emotionally, not a drop of stress in my body, and I'd still hear them. I'd still know they were sneaking around, trying to steal my opportunity. So it has absolutely nothing to do with how stressed I am or if my mood is up or down. It just stays right there with me, day after day, for weeks at a time, because it's the truth of what's happening.

Can you think of any time when your belief about being watched or having your work judged was challenged directly by something you experienced yourself, not just what others said, and if so, did it change your belief at all?

Well, doctor, I know we keep circling back around to this, and I feel like I'm just talking your ear off about the exact same thing, but it’s just... it's my life, you know? It's what I'm dealing with every single day. You're asking if I ever saw something with my own two eyes that should have made me think differently. And, well, yes, I suppose I did try to play detective myself once. 

Because, like I was just saying a few minutes ago, I got it so deep in my head that the other home-care agency and those specific people from the library were watching my paintings and snooping around my client papers. I knew they were doing it to steal a chance that was meant for me, and me alone. I just knew it. So, one morning before I went over to help Mrs. Gable—she’s another one of my clients, sweet lady, but she needs a whole lot of help getting her compression socks on, it takes me a good twenty minutes just to get them over her heels—I decided to set a little trap. I took a single strand of hair from my hairbrush, just one little gray hair, and I laid it ever so carefully right across my client logs and my watercolor pad on the kitchen table. I figured, if they are coming in here to look at my things, they'll brush that hair right off and I'll know for sure. 

Well, I came home after a long, long day. My feet were just aching, I was bone tired. I walked in, didn't even take my coat off, and went straight over to that table. And doctor, the hair was exactly where I left it. Not moved a fraction of an inch. Everything was completely untouched. 

So there it was, right? My own little test showing nothing. And you know, even when folks told me it made no sense before, and now here I was looking at my own test that made it seem like nobody had been there... I still knew they were doing it. It didn't change my mind one single bit. I just stood there looking at that piece of hair and thought, well, they must be using tiny cameras, or they have some way of looking through the windows when I'm not paying attention, or they're just getting more clever about it. Because you can't tell me it isn't happening. I don't care if the hair didn't move, and I don't care if it seems to make no sense to anyone else. I know they are watching my work to take my opportunity, and absolutely nothing I see or don't see is going to wipe that truth away.
Can you think of any experience, even a small one, that made you doubt your belief, even for a moment, that you were being watched or that your work was being judged?

Doctor, I feel like we are just going round and round in circles today, I really do. You keep asking if I ever doubted it, if there was even one tiny little second where I thought, well, maybe I am just imagining things. And I have to tell you, the answer is just plain no. 

Because, like I have been trying to explain to you this whole time, I got it in my head that the other home-care agency—the ones who drive those awful bright green vans around town—and some of those people from the library were watching my paintings and my client papers. And they aren't just doing it for fun, they are doing it to steal a chance that was meant for me. That is my chance, my opportunity, after all my years of hard work as an aide, wiping down counters and lifting heavy patients and making sure everyone else is taken care of. 

I have had plenty of people try to talk me out of it, so it's not like I haven't heard the other side. It's not just my sister or Mrs. Higgins trying to play detective. My supervisor at work, Brenda, she sat me down in the breakroom just last week. That breakroom always smells like burnt popcorn because nobody watches the microwave, but anyway, Brenda sat me down and she talked to me for nearly an hour. She brought up every reason under the sun why she thought I was wrong. She told me it made absolutely no sense for anyone at a library to care about my watercolor paintings or my daily client logs. She went on and on about how everyone is just too busy with their own lives to be tracking mine.

But even when folks like Brenda and my sister told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. I didn't doubt it for a single moment, doctor. Not one. Because when you know the truth, when you live with it every day and you see how they are trying to take what is rightfully yours, someone telling you it doesn't make sense just sounds like foolishness. You could bring the whole town in here to tell me I'm wrong, and I would still know exactly what they are up to. So no, no doubts at all. Not even a small one.
Have there ever been two full weeks in a row when you did not experience any of these voices or the feeling of being watched or targeted?

Two full weeks? Oh, doctor, I wish. I really, truly wish I could sit here and tell you that I got a break like that, even just for a few days, let alone two whole weeks. But no, there hasn't been a break at all. Not a single one. Because... well, if I really sit back and count the time, these voices talking about me, and those fixed fears I have about my work being watched and judged—it has been happening for about nine months now. Nine whole months, doctor. 

I remember because it was right around the time I had to buy my new white non-slip shoes for my shifts. I was doing a lot of mornings with Mr. Henderson back then, and you know how hard it is on your feet, standing on that hard linoleum all day, making sure he doesn't slip in the bathroom. I remember bringing those shoes home, setting them by the front door, and that's when it really settled in. The whispering. The feeling of eyes just boring into the back of my neck while I was doing my client logs. And since that day, nine months ago, it hasn't stopped for a weekend, it hasn't stopped for a holiday, it hasn't stopped for a single week, let alone two. 

It's just a constant, everyday thing now. You wake up, you make your chamomile tea, you hear them. You go to work, you wipe down the counters, you feel them watching your every move. Month after month after month. So when you ask if I've had two weeks without it, I just have to shake my head, because nine months is a long time to carry this around every single minute of the day. They are just relentless, they really are, and I keep trying to explain to people how exhausting it is to have your work scrutinized like that for almost a whole year, but nobody seems to... well, nobody seems to grasp just how long nine months really feels when you're going through it.
Can you think of any time when you believed something so strongly that, even when you saw clear proof it wasn’t true, you still knew in your heart that it was?

Well, doctor, I feel like we are just beating a dead horse here, because that's exactly what I've been trying to tell you this whole entire time. We keep coming back to this idea of proof, but what does 'clear proof' even mean when you just know something in your bones? 

I mean, I already told you about the little hair I left on the table, and how it didn't move. And I told you about Brenda talking my ear off in the breakroom, trying to give me all her reasons and her 'proof' that I was wrong. But... well, like I said, I got it in my head that the other home-care agency and some of those people from the library were watching my paintings and my client papers. And they were doing it to steal a chance that was meant for me. My chance! After all my years of breaking my back for my clients, washing them and making sure they take their pills, this was my one opportunity, and they wanted to snatch it. 

And you see, even when I did my own test and it showed nothing, or even when folks told me it made absolutely no sense and tried to show me how impossible it was... I still knew they were doing it. It didn't matter what I saw with my own eyes or what anybody else said to me. When you know something that deep in your heart, when you can just feel them trying to take what is rightfully yours, no amount of so-called proof is going to change your mind. I just knew they were doing it, doctor, plain and simple, and no piece of evidence was ever going to make me believe otherwise.
Have you ever had a time when you were clearly shown that one of your beliefs was wrong, and if so, did that change how you thought about other similar beliefs you had?

Doctor, I... I honestly don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you today. I feel like a broken record, I really do. You keep asking me about being shown I was wrong and if it changed my mind about other things, but you're missing the whole point. You're assuming I ever believed their so-called proof in the first place! 

Like I've been telling you all morning, I got it firmly in my head that the other home-care agency—the ones with those loud green vans—and those specific people from the library were watching my paintings and snooping on my client papers. And I know exactly why they were doing it. They were trying to steal a chance that was meant for me. My one big opportunity! After all the years I've spent working as an aide, breaking my back lifting people, making sure they don't slip in the shower, keeping track of every little thing on those logs... I earned that chance. 

So when folks sat me down, like Brenda did, and tried to tell me it made absolutely no sense for library workers to care about my watercolors or my daily logs... well, it didn't change my mind about that, and it certainly didn't make me question anything else I knew to be true. Why would it? If someone tries to tell you the sky is green, you don't suddenly start doubting that the grass is green too, do you? You just know they're talking nonsense. Even when folks told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. I knew it right down to my toes.
